subject.title: [Security] Missing CSRF protection on local control plane HTTP routes

question: Does the shipped shared browser-origin gate cover every state-changing Gateway HTTP route relevant to this report, or is there a distinct route or authentication mode that also requires token-based CSRF protection?
rationale: The issue has a protected security label, and deciding whether origin validation is sufficient versus requiring anti-CSRF tokens affects trusted-proxy and headless-client security contracts; that policy choice cannot be inferred safely from the route names in the report.

options.title: Confirm coverage and close
options.body: Verify all state-changing HTTP routes traverse the shared origin-aware authorization seam, then close this issue as already addressed by the v2026.3.31 fix.

options.title: Keep for narrow route audit
options.body: Request one concrete route-level reproduction and patch the shared Gateway HTTP boundary if that route bypasses existing origin validation.

options.title: Require CSRF tokens
options.body: Define a new browser-session CSRF-token contract for state-changing HTTP routes, accepting the compatibility and client-integration work this creates.

recommendation.title: Confirm coverage and close
recommendation.body: Verify all state-changing HTTP routes traverse the shared origin-aware authorization seam, then close this issue as already addressed by the v2026.3.31 fix.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the existing shared HTTP-origin security boundary and are best positioned to confirm its intended coverage.
